summary: Baidu authors build an automated generator of repository-level code-understanding questions for 10 SWE-bench Python repositories. A tool agent (read_file, list_directory, regex search_code) starts from a selected documentation chunk and writes a code-grounded gold answer. LLM checks strip claims that only the documentation supports, and a question plus rubric are then derived from the answer. Four frontier models answer 528 'code-derivable' and 100 'doc-dependent' questions with the same agent under three conditions: closed-book, code-only (docstrings, comments and doc files stripped) and documented. A GPT-5.4 judge scores the answers. Code access adds about +0.23 to +0.36 over closed-book. Documentation adds +0.071 on doc-dependent tasks and roughly nothing on code-derivable tasks.

claims.claim: Code access is the dominant factor (+0.23 mean gain over closed-book).
claims.evidence: Table 5 (doc-dependent): 0.629->0.860 (+0.231). Table 6 (code-derivable): 0.500->0.857 (+0.357). Paired bootstrap over tasks gives p<0.001 for all models. Caveats: one run per model and condition, a single unvalidated LLM judge, and famous repositories, so closed-book is inflated by memorization (0.44-0.68). Closed-book is a weak comparator for a private codebase.

claims.claim: Documentation provides a modest additional benefit (+0.071 on doc-dependent tasks, p<0.003).
claims.evidence: Table 5 shows +0.053 to +0.091 across models. But doc-dependent gold answers were 'produced in a single LLM turn from documentation only (no code tools)' and were not code-verified (§4.5), so the documented arm is graded against doc-derived text by construction. The documented condition also gets a different system prompt telling the agent to search the docs first (§6.1), which confounds doc presence with instructions.

claims.claim: Code-only is about equal to documented on code-derivable tasks (delta < 0.01), validating the design.
claims.evidence: The mean delta is +0.006 (Table 6), but Claude scores +0.026 (p<0.001, attributed to generator advantage) and Gemini -0.018 (p=0.004). The authors concede in §8 that the near-zero delta is 'partially self-confirming', because the tasks were filtered to be code-answerable.

claims.claim: Answer-first generation ensures every task is grounded in real code structure with verified gold answers.
claims.evidence: Verification is LLM-only. The fact-check passes 38.4% of answers and gives 61.6% 'warn', and warned tasks are retained. There is no human validation of gold answers (Limitations).

claims.claim: Generator-evaluatee bias is negligible on the primary metric.
claims.evidence: The only evidence is DeepSeek 0.892 vs Claude 0.891 in code-only on code-derivable tasks. Claude (the gold-answer generator) leads in the documented and closed-book conditions, and the authors attribute its significant +0.026 to generator advantage.

patterns.note: Comparison: a 60-turn tool agent with read/list/regex search vs closed-book (no repository). The agent wins by +0.23 to +0.36 on famous Python libraries, reaching 0.77-0.89 on a judged 0-1 scale. Closed-book is a weak alternative for private code, where memorization would be near zero. There is no comparison against RAG, code graphs, a different agent design or human answers. Scores sit near ceiling.

Comparison: prose documentation (docstrings, comments, README/docs) present vs stripped, same agent. Doc-dependent tasks gain +0.071, partly by construction because their gold answers were written from the docs. Code-derivable tasks gain about 0; the only significant category is 'Where' (+0.011, d=0.13), suggesting docs act as a navigation index. Gemini drops -0.018 with docs present, which the authors attribute to turn budget spent reading docs. This is natural-language docs, not structured cards or contracts.
Retrieval is regex search plus file reads only. It is sufficient for high scores here, but no alternative retrieval is compared.
A single GPT-5.4 rubric judge with no inter-judge or human agreement study (acknowledged). The specificity axis saturates at >=4.78/5 whenever the agent has repository access.
The What/Why/Where/How taxonomy matches the questions a developer asks before writing a spec, but the paper measures answer quality only, not whether discovery improves downstream specs or code.
Automated benchmark synthesis over SWE-bench repositories with a three-condition contamination design.

methodology.sample: 528 code-derivable and 100 doc-dependent tasks across 10 pinned SWE-bench Python repositories, balanced 25% per What/Why/Where/How category.
methodology.baselines: Closed-book (no repository) and documented vs code-only conditions. No alternative agent or retrieval design.
methodology.models: Claude Opus 4.6 (also the task generator), DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi-K2.6, Gemini-3.1-Pro, all with the same built-in agent (60 turns, 4,096 max tokens). The judge is GPT-5.4.
methodology.variance: Paired bootstrap CIs over tasks with Bonferroni correction. Single run per model and condition. No judge-repeat variance.
methodology.ablations: The three conditions, a per-axis breakdown, and a 2-axis composite without specificity (App. I). No identifier-obfuscation ablation (left to future work).
methodology.contamination_controls: Doc stripping plus a closed-book condition to quantify memorization. The repositories are famous, and closed-book reaches 0.44-0.68.

standards.artifacts: The paper says the framework is open-source but gives no URL. The code-only verification prompt is in App. E.

biases.detail: A single GPT-5.4 judge with no human correlation or inter-judge agreement (authors' own limitation).
Doc-dependent gold answers are derived from the documentation, so 'documentation utility' is measured against doc-authored answers. Specificity saturates and adds no signal in agentic conditions.
The documented condition tells the agent to search the docs first, while code-only tells it docs were stripped. Condition deltas therefore mix doc presence with instructions.
Claude Opus 4.6 generates the gold answers and is also evaluated. It leads two of the three conditions.
SWE-bench repositories are heavily represented in pretraining. Closed-book scores of 0.44-0.68 show substantial memorization, which inflates every condition.
Ten Python repositories. The doc-stripping method is Python-AST-specific.
'Open-source' is claimed without a repository link.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Anthropic, DeepSeek, Moonshot and Google models. No Baidu model is evaluated.
coi.detail: Vendor affiliation only. The authors do not rank a product of their own.

verdict_reason: A useful design idea (closed-book / code-only / documented deltas) with task-level CIs across four models. But the documentation-utility headline is partly built in, because doc-dependent gold answers come from the docs and the documented arm gets a different prompt. The validation delta is self-confirming, gold answers and scoring rest on unvalidated LLMs, and everything is Python on famous repositories.
applicability: For onboarding developers who lack domain knowledge, the transferable finding is that a plain tool agent (grep-style search plus file reads, no index) answers What/Where/How questions about large repositories well when it reads the code. Prose documentation mainly adds completeness on rationale and caveat questions, and helps locate features. A codebase-QA agent across the 4+ the repositories is therefore worth piloting before writing agent-facing documentation in bulk. The doc-dependent category (design rationale, deprecations, edge-case caveats) is exactly where the domain rules and upstream content-provider contracts live, so code alone will fall short there. That shortfall will likely be larger in private Java code, where models have memorized nothing. The answer-first recipe (an agent explores code, writes an answer with file evidence, then derives the question) is a cheap way to build an onboarding quiz or eval set from the team's own repositories, but answers need human checking: this paper's gold answers were 61.6% 'warn'. Gemini's negative doc effect is a caution against harness prompts that force 'read the docs first' under a turn budget.

conflicts_with.detail: Apparent tension. In that paper, delivering AGENTS.md context (always-on or via on-demand wiki) had no detectable effect on patch correctness. Here, documentation significantly improves answers on doc-dependent questions (+0.071). The two reconcile by task type: repository docs help when the needed fact (rationale, caveats) is absent from code, and add about nothing when the code itself suffices, which is the code-derivable result here.
